title: Dimarco talks open
description: Saturday, September 12, 2026: Gazzetta dello Sport reports Inter have opened talks on a contract to 2030 for Federico Dimarco, Chivu's press conference is set for Sunday, and John Stones is in line to start against Udinese.
mast_alt: Nerazzurri Daily Edition No. 11, Saturday, September 12, 2026 — Dimarco talks open

blocks.html: Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Inter have opened talks on a new contract for Federico Dimarco through 2030. Chivu takes questions on Sunday at 8:00 AM ET (14:00 CEST), a time the club has now set, and the same paper has John Stones starting on Monday with Josep Martinez keeping the gloves. Inter themselves have published nothing about the team.

rows.label: TODAY
rows.name: No match
rows.line: SERIE A · 9 POINTS FROM 3 · LEVEL AT THE TOP

blocks.h3: Chivu speaks Sunday, and it is streamed
paras: Inter's own communiqué sets Cristian Chivu's pre-match press conference for Sunday, September 13 at 8:00 AM ET (14:00 CEST), at the Inter Training Center in Appiano Gentile. The club says it will be streamed live on its official channels.
Inter have published no lineup and no injury list. Everything under the red bar is press.

blocks.h3: Akanji signs off from Manchester City
paras: Manuel Akanji posted a farewell to Manchester City on Instagram late on Friday, thanking the coach, his teammates and the staff for what he called three incredible years. He had trained with the Inter squad at Appiano Gentile that same morning.

blocks.h3: Gazzetta: talks open on Dimarco to 2030
paras: Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Inter and Federico Dimarco have started negotiating an extension to 2030, with a meeting set between sporting director Dario Baccin and the player's agent, Arturo Canales. His current deal runs to 2027 with a club option for one more year, and the paper puts his salary at about €4 million net a season.
blocks.kicker: GAZZETTA DELLO SPORT VIA FCINTERNEWS · SEP 12

blocks.h3: Gazzetta: Stones starts, Martinez keeps the gloves
paras: The same paper has John Stones starting in the middle of the defense against Udinese, with Manuel Akanji back from muscle fatigue. Josep Martinez stays in goal despite the error that led to Madrid's opening goal; Gazzetta writes that Chivu weighed a change to Ivan Provedel and decided against it for now.
Up front the question is Marcus Thuram, whom the paper puts at 60 to 70 percent, against Pio Esposito. Dimarco has still not rejoined full group training.
